doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: How Billy met Mary in 1909 and their marriage
summary: Billy tells how he formed a minstrel-style boys' show, joined a theater in Bay St. Louis, went to New Orleans for a girl who could talk and found Mary after her Lincoln Park engagement. They married in Mobile in 1909.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Prince's Family Theatre, Youngstown, Ohio. Now, can you tell me when you first met your wife, Mr. Brian? Oh, yes. It was in

the year of... 19... 1908. 1909. Were you in the entertainment field? Oh, yes. I started out with this little company that she joined later in 1908, but I didn't actually meet her until 1909. And I took the company out with all men, all boys. Of course, I was not a boy myself. Yes, sir. But I somehow, I had a... No show people in my family, but I just had that inclination to be a showman. And I got together these boys and started out with a little menstrual style show, which later became a kind of a presentation show. Yes. And we didn't have any girls whatsoever until we met a man that was stranded down in a little town called Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. Oh, yes, I know that. You do. And there was a little theater there, and he had the theater in charge, but he couldn't carry on so very well. I mean, we joined up with the theater. And, uh, uh, coming around the town that we still wanted to make the show a little larger. In fact, we needed a girl that could talk. And so I went to New Orleans to see if we could get some girls, which was about 51 miles from Bay St. Louis. And that's where I met my wife. Somebody directed me to this girl. And I found her early one morning after she had come from a singing engagement out at the fairgrounds, was it?
Lincoln Park. Oh, yeah, Lincoln Park. Yeah. Yes.

Did you play or sing with Robichaux out there? Yes. I know he played there for many years. Buddy Bartley, he did the balloon ascension. Yes. Professor Minetta has told us all about those too. Yes. Yes. One time he went up too far and, uh, and he got lost. He went over in the lake. Yes, yes, yes, yes.

Well, then that's how we met. And then, uh, we went to Bay St. Louis. He taken me to Bay St. Louis. And, uh, then we went to Mobile and that's where we married. Mobile, Alabama. In 1909, about? In 1909. We've been together. The Haley's Comet was along that line there. I remember that. When I was a boy is one of the first things I can remember.
Yeah. And I was in my teens then, you know. Yeah. It was just, just, uh, 18th Wednesday had just passed
